messages:
alice: Heads-up — after yesterday's allocator tweak (reduce fragmentation by merging small arenas) some prod workers report prompt-cache pressure and occasional OOMs on long-context workloads. Wasn't obvious in unit tests.

bob: which workers / models? any correlation with sequence length distribution?

alice: r5b-prod cluster, mostly gpt-like 32k models. Spike in resident GPU usage when prefix-cache hit-rate drops under ~18% during bursty multi-turns. Root msg at 1796004321.

carla: can you paste the short profiler snapshot? even rough numbers help.

alice: sure, quick snippet from `nvprof`-style sampling around the event:
```
Timestamp  GPU_mem_MB  active_allocators  kv_cache_usage_MB  workspace_MB  oom_count
17:03:21   38120       6                  12480              6200          1
17:03:24   39216       8                  13600              6200          0
```
Note `kv_cache_usage_MB` jumps after a failed prefix lookup -> fallback to full prefetch.

yusuf: interesting. The allocator merge probably increased max contiguous free block but also raised worst-case peak because we delay recycling of small buffers. So transient prefetch spikes can't reuse tiny buffers fast enough.

nina: two knobs to consider: (1) aggressive TTL eviction for low-access shards, (2) keep a small slab pool for small prefix entries to avoid touching big arenas. TTL param we used was `prefix_ttl_ms: 300000` — maybe too long for low-cardinality shards.

carla: agree. Also check batching heuristics — when we batch many short requests we end up with larger combined KV prefetch per batch. Kernel selection matters too: some kernels require workspace growth with batch size.

alice: did a micro-benchmark of three configs this morning (same traffic replay):
- baseline (old allocator) => 8 OOMs in 24h window, avg mem 36500MB
- merged-arenas (current) => 22 OOMs, avg peak 39000MB
- merged + small-slab (experiment) => 3 OOMs, avg peak 37200MB

bob: small-slab looks promising. Any perf reg on latency?

yusuf: latency 99p increased by ~3ms with small-slab, likely due to an extra allocator path on miss. But P50/P90 unchanged.

nina: propose rollout plan: enable small-slab allocator on a canary pool + lower TTL for tails to 60s for shards with hit-rate < 25%. Also add metric `prefix_shard_rebalance_attempts` to track churn.

carla: also add a guard in kernel selection layer: if predicted workspace growth > 20% for current batch, prefer kernel B (lower workspace, slightly higher compute) — that reduces peak memory during prefetch-heavy bursts.

alice: I'll push a canary with small-slab + TTL tweak. Patch referenced in PR: `git@repo:redwood/engine#2345` — includes tests and a new synthetic workload that stresses 32k seq prefetch.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled by alice to r5b-canary at 1796004360. Rolling 3 nodes.

bob: once canary is up, run the replay twice (baseline trace + 2x burst) and upload `nvprof` snapshots to the thread.

alice: will do. Early results from a tiny canary run show peak down ~8% and no OOMs in 30m burst. Will report full run by 1796004395.

carla: if this holds, we should consider a scheduler-level prefetch budget: cap per-request prefetch to X MB or throttle batch size when per-batch predicted prefetch sum > budget. Keeps memory predictable.

yusuf: +1. Also track `kv_cache_eviction_rate` to catch oscillation loops.

alice: noted. Thanks everyone :thumbsup: Will post the full trace and the nvprof dumps shortly.
